title: Violinists and early trumpeters: George Jones, Fester Manetta, Buddy Bolden
summary: Nash names violin and bass players, a contest-winning band, and the trumpeters before Armstrong, Bolden, Bunk Johnson, Kid Rena, Buddy Petit.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Do you remember anybody in particular who used to play in these? In Spanos or Savokas?
Spanos? Well, yes. An old friend of mine, George Jones, a violin player, he died some time ago. Yeah, George Jones, he died. Is that the same guy playing the bass violin?

That was Cornelius. No, no, that's George Jones who played the bass violin. You're right, Cornelius played the violin. That's right, he died. Yeah, he was a good violin player. He came up the time of Fester Monette over in Algea, across the river. All those guys were great violin players, you know. Fester Monette, Cornelius, and Fester Clayborne William out of Donisonville. They came there once and won the contest. Yeah, they won the contest here playing once. They had a very, very good band. And then, all the trumpet players, the best trumpet players they had around here, back in the back of those days, was a fellow around there that used to call Buddy Bolin. He was a great trumpet player, you see. He was way before Lou Armstrong time, Buddy Bolin was. He was a great trumpet player. And after Buddy Bolin, Buddy Bolin, and Bunk Johnson, all them fellas around, came up around the same time. And this other fella, Kid Randy, Buddy P.T., and Jack Carey, the kid's son, and all them fellas, they came along behind these fellas. At the time.
